title: Our Services
text:
Research
We design rigorous, transparent research using open-source tools and reproducible methods, so your findings hold up and your stakeholders can trust them. We employ both quantitative and qualitative methods in the social sciences - from predictive analytics to focus groups and interviews.

title: Our Services
text:
Data Strategy
We help leaders turn scattered data into a clear roadmap: what to measure, how to collect it, and how to use it to guide decisions and investment. We enable organizational digital transformation through the entire enterprise application architecture - from core system, to data warehousing, to stakeholder-facing data products.

title: Our Services
text:
Visualization & Storytelling
We transform complex data into clear, compelling visual narratives that make your work understandable and actionable for any audience. We believe data have a story to tell and we make sure the value of the data is not lost in statistical jargon.

title: Our Services
text:
Program Evaluation
We evaluate programs with rigor and care, measuring what matters so you can demonstrate impact, learn quickly, and improve over time. We ground our work in theory and harness the latest science to make sure your theory of change is achievable.

title: Our Services
text:
Data Engineering
We build the pipelines and infrastructure behind good analysis, turning messy, siloed data into reliable, well-organized systems your team can count on. Sourcing data from different systems and different files can be a large task we can help automate.

title: Our Services
text:
Data Governance
We establish practical standards for data quality, privacy, and ethics, so your data is handled responsibly and trusted across your organization. Building a positive data culture at your organization strengthens the foundations of your outcomes.

title: Our Services
text:
Consulting
We act as your on-demand data partner, bringing flexible, senior-level expertise to whatever challenge is in front of you — from a single question to a full transformation. Whether you need a thought partner for a board presentation or an embedded analyst for a multi-year initiative, we meet you where you are.

title: Our Services
text:
Areas of Expertise





Criminal Legal System

We bring deep expertise in criminology, deviance, and social control to research on courts, policing, incarceration, and reentry. Our work helps agencies and advocates understand system behavior, measure outcomes, and inform policies that promote fairness and public safety.




K-12 Education

We understand the data landscape of schools and districts, from student achievement and attendance to discipline disparities and family engagement. Our analyses help educators and administrators identify what’s working, for whom, and where to focus resources.




Higher Education

We study enrollment, persistence, completion, and student success across institutional contexts. Our research helps colleges and universities make evidence-based decisions about access, equity, and program effectiveness - not just national rankings.




Demographic Analysis

We are experts in census data, population estimates, and the methods for understanding who lives in a place and how communities are changing. We translate demographic shifts into planning-ready insight for organizations and agencies.




Survey Methods

We design surveys that measure what they intend to measure, applying best practices in sampling, question construction, and instrument validation. From design to analysis, we ensure your data is credible and defensible.




Data Visualization

We are steeped in the theory and craft of visual communication, grounded in research on perception and decision-making. We design visuals that are not only beautiful, but honest, accessible, and effective at driving understanding.

title: About Us
text:
Emily Knaphus-Soran, PhD





Emily Knaphus-Soran, Principal & Co-Founder





Emily Knaphus-Soran is a sociologist by training who was drawn to evaluation through a desire to support on-the-ground efforts that address the social problems illuminated by sociological research. She has been conducting equity-focused research and evaluation for over a decade, beginning with graduate studies centered on the persistence of mass incarceration and its intergenerational social-psychological impacts. Her graduate training equipped her with the tools to conduct rigorous quantitative and qualitative applied research and evaluation. Emily earned her PhD in sociology from the University of Washington in 2017, with a minor in social statistics and a graduate certificate in socio-legal studies.
She has worked as an evaluator for more than ten years, both in her role at the University of Washington Center for Evaluation & Research for STEM Equity (UW CERSE) and as an independent consultant. She has managed the evaluation of several NSF-funded programs, including efforts both within single institutions and across multiple institutions. She has also conducted evaluations of programs designed as alternatives to arrest and incarceration and contributed to evaluation-capacity building with a ten-site cohort building alternatives to criminal-legal responses to behaviors stemming from unmet behavioral health needs.
To learn more about her professional experience, see Emily’s curriculum vitae.

title: About Us
text:
Jorge Martinez





Jorge Martinez, Principal & Co-Founder





Jorge Martinez is a researcher, data strategist, and co-founder of Common Measure. Trained as a sociologist with a focus on deviance and social control, Jorge spent nearly a decade as an institutional researcher in higher education at the University of Houston where he turned enrollment trends, survey research, and predictive modeling into actionable insight, including work on retention analytics and university benchmarking. He later brought that analytical rigor to the K-12 sector, applying data science to support one of the nation’s largest school districts. Today, as Director of Data Strategy at BakerRipley, he leads a team of researchers and data scientists supporting socioeconomic mobility work across the Houston region—an experience that keeps him steeped in the real challenges nonprofits face, from measuring program outcomes to communicating results to funders and boards. He brings that practitioner’s perspective to every Common Measure engagement, pairing rigorous research design and statistical analysis with data visualization that makes findings impossible to ignore. Jorge holds an MA in Sociology from the University of Washington and completed doctoral coursework in sociology there (ABD). Outside of work, you’ll find him cycling around Houston, exploring museums, learning new R packages, or spending time with his pug.
To learn more about his professional experience, see Jorge’s curriculum vitae or visit his website to see some of his work.
